Given
\[
|\psi\rangle=\frac12|\uparrow\rangle+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}|\downarrow\rangle,
\]
the probabilities are \(\frac14\) and \(\frac34\).

\[
\langle\sigma_z\rangle=\frac14-\frac34=-\frac12.
\]

Since the coefficients are real,
\[
\langle\sigma_x\rangle
=2\left(\frac12\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)
=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]

Thus,
\[
\langle10\sigma_z+5\sigma_x\rangle
=10\left(-\frac12\right)+5\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)
=-5+\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}
\approx -0.67.
\]

To one decimal place, this is \(-0.7\).

Answer: A
